content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I have a [product_name] CPU [article_no] with a memory card and I'm considering purchasing a spare unit in case of malfunction. I recently found out that this CPU model has been discontinued and the replacement is [article_no]. My question is: If I buy the new CPU and swap it with the old one, using the same memory card that currently holds the program, will it function properly?

Yes, it should work. However, it's recommended to upgrade to the latest [product_name] software [version_no], as the updated CPU is compatible with it. Without updating to [product_name] [version_no], certain features such as connectivity and program transfer may not be available, and some parameters may be inaccessible. The selection of devices in the program file is also dependent on the software version. You can download the upgrade from [url], but note that it is subject to export restrictions and requires extended registration. Registration explains what information is necessary for downloading restricted software.

Thank you. I forgot to mention that my CPU is connected to two digital input/output modules and three analog input modules. Does your previous answer still apply regarding compatibility with these modules?
Yes, the expansion modules with [article_no] as part of their article numbers are compatible with all CPUs from the [version_no] series.

I have one more question. The current program on my CPU is password-protected by the manufacturer, and I do not have the password. If I move the memory card from the old CPU to the new one, will the new CPU be able to run the existing program without needing to rewrite it? My goal is a quick repair without modifying the program.

Yes, the programmed memory card should work in the new CPU. However, without the correct software version, you will not be able to modify the program or establish an online connection. Those actions require [product_name] [version_no].

analysis.insight_summary: Users seek clarity on hardware compatibility and straightforward program migration when replacing a [product_name] with its updated version, particularly when there are software version differences. There is concern about whether a password-protected program on a memory card will function correctly on a new CPU, as well as whether all modules are supported. The importance of using the matching [product_name] software version, especially [version_no], is emphasized for connectivity and program adjustments.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that transferring a memory card to a new [product_name] will allow the system to operate immediately, with all expansion modules working seamlessly. They hope to avoid rewriting programs due to password restrictions and expect minimal additional configuration following hardware replacement.
